knowledge_gaps: PAD-hole corruption changes attention eligibility as well as item content. Patching a deleted token’s residual does not restore its masked key/value access, so restoration and disruption are not symmetric interventions. The report must distinguish content replacement from deletion and specify the recipient attention mask.

The patch location needs an architecture-specific definition: layer index, pre/post normalization, tensor layout, and selected positions. Patching history-token outputs after the final attention block cannot affect the appended-MASK readout through positionwise operations. A shallow backbone may therefore offer few informative patch locations.

Reproduction requires fixed corruption rules, prefix selection, layer/token selection, candidate sampling, deterministic tie-breaking, effect signs, numerical tolerances, and bootstrap procedures. Random controls must also match token eligibility; matching position range alone is insufficient.

The hardest-negative margin measures top-1 separation rather than the host’s HR@10 boundary, and the maximizing negative can change between interventions. Report rank and hit@10 alongside it, and distinguish fixed-competitor from maximum-negative effects.

The proposal lacks a prespecified route from localization to a training repair and a diagnostic runtime cap. Exploring many layers, positions, and corruptions risks selective reporting; repeatedly selecting repairs on the same validation sample introduces adaptive overfitting. Future potential 8 and difficulty 4 are optimistic until these issues are resolved; originality 5 is plausible for an adaptation.
